reference: Every circuit re-derived from its topology and implemented independently in python: mass balance and enthalpy balance written separately at each junction, emitter output from the EN 442 relation with the logarithmic excess temperature solved by scipy.optimize.brentq, water properties from iapws 1.5.5 (IAPWS-IF97 region 1) at 0.3 MPa, valve authority and the installed characteristic from their published definitions. The tool is driven through the DOM only.
reference_citations: EN 442-2, heat output of radiators and convectors: Q/Q_n = (dT/dT_n)^n with dT the logarithmic excess temperature and the 75/65/20 rating point (dT_n = 49.83 K)

CIBSE Guide H: Building control systems, CIBSE, London, 2009, ISBN 978-1-906846-00-8, section 3.3.4.1 eq. (3.5): valve authority N = pressure drop across the fully open valve / pressure difference available to the controlled branch; section 3.3.3.1 eq. (3.1)-(3.2) for the equal-percentage characteristic
ASHRAE Handbook — HVAC Systems and Equipment (2016), ch. 47 "Valves", modulating authority range 0.25 to 0.5
IAPWS R7-97 (2012), region 1, as implemented by python-iapws 1.5.5
BSRIA BG 49/2015, Commissioning water systems — the same authority definition and the balancing procedure the cards describe
tolerance: Circuit temperatures are compared to 0.05 degC and flows to 0.005 m3/h — half of the tool's own printed unit in each case, which is the tightest demand its display can carry. Balances (mass and enthalpy) are required to close to 1e-12 kg/s and 1e-6 W on the reference, and to within the two printed digits on the numbers the tool shows. Valve characteristics are exact algebra: 1e-12. The water-property comparison is limited by the printed precision of the flow (2e-3 relative) and is stated as such.

Card C1 at 100 % load. Through the UI the primary flow is wired at 1.1x the secondary (C1, C2) or exactly equal to it (C3), so the bypass can only run supply -> return: the secondary supply must be the undiluted primary temperature and the mixing must appear on the primary return alone.

Card C2 at 100 % load. Through the UI the primary flow is wired at 1.1x the secondary (C1, C2) or exactly equal to it (C3), so the bypass can only run supply -> return: the secondary supply must be the undiluted primary temperature and the mixing must appear on the primary return alone.

Card C3 at 100 % load. Through the UI the primary flow is wired at 1.1x the secondary (C1, C2) or exactly equal to it (C3), so the bypass can only run supply -> return: the secondary supply must be the undiluted primary temperature and the mixing must appear on the primary return alone.

A header carrying a surplus (C1/C2, primary 1.1x secondary) mixes primary supply water into its primary return, so that return must be WARMER than the one of the balanced manifold C3, which carries no cross flow at all. Same load, same design.

The page runs its own checks in the browser on every input change and prints them. They are a self-check: every one of them re-evaluates this page's own formulas (mass and enthalpy balance round its own circuits, the sign of each trend, the authority identities) and none compares against an outside implementation. They are counted here, not credited as validation. 7 checks, 0 failing.

The tool serves h(T) from a 0.05 K table built from IF97 region 1 with linear interpolation. Its design mass flow Q/(h(75) - h(65)) is recovered from the printed network flow of circuit A1 at full load and compared with iapws 1.5.5. The comparison is limited by the printed precision of the flow (0.01 m3/h), not by the water model.

enthalpy_difference_75_65.unit: J/kg (tolerance 7.86e-5 = half a printed 0.01 m3/h on 174.85 m3/h, plus 5e-5 for the tool's 0.05 K enthalpy table)

provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_hydraulicsolutions.py from the sources this artifact cites. That generator was re-run on 2026-10-16 with iapws 1.5.5 installed, in a reference directory from which hydraulicsolutions_ref.json had first been removed, and wrote a file byte-identical to the deployed corpus (140 000 B); so no case reuses a stored reference that this tree cannot re-derive.
